candidate_relations.reason: Chondrosarcoma of the skull implies a primary cranial cartilage tumor rather than metastatic extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma from the foot.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: primary skull chondrosarcoma vs metastatic EMC

candidate_relations.reason: Metastatic tumor fits a lytic diploic mass after remote sarcoma but omits extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma.
Plasmacytoma is a plasma-cell neoplasm, not suggested by a gray circumscribed mass in a man with known EMC.
Metastatic extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma is the same tumor as the reference, now a right frontal diploic mass 9 years after foot EMC.
Bone tumor describes the lytic frontal lesion without specifying extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma.
Primary osteosarcoma of the skull is a bone-forming primary, conflicting with metastatic EMC after below-knee amputation.
Extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma is the reference diagnosis for this late cranial recurrence of the treated foot tumor.
Osteosarcoma is a distinct osteogenic sarcoma, not the myxoid chondrosarcoma lineage of the prior foot primary.
Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans is a cutaneous fibroblastic tumor unrelated to this diploic lytic mass.
No hyperparathyroidism is described to support a brown tumor of the skull.
Soft-tissue sarcoma is the parent family of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma and lacks that specificity.
Metastatic disease is compatible with intracranial-extending lytic bone disease but does not name EMC.
Adjuvant therapy was ifosfamide–doxorubicin without radiation, so radiation-induced osteosarcoma does not apply.
The referring lipoma diagnosis is contradicted by a lytic diploic origin with intracranial extension and a bony step-off.
Aneurysmal bone cyst is a benign cystic bone lesion, not a solid gray mass in a patient with prior EMC.
Minor forehead trauma is a red herring; CT shows a lytic diploic lesion rather than a purely traumatic collection.
Metastatic myxoid chondrosarcoma of the skull is the same EMC now involving frontal diploë and possible superior sagittal sinus.
Giant-cell tumor of the skull is a primary osteoclast-rich bone tumor, not metastatic extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma.
Chordoma arises from notochordal remnants, typically clivus/sacrum, not the right frontal diploic space.

case_quality_flags: The forehead mass was not resected or biopsied; metastatic EMC is inferred from remote foot EMC plus a lytic diploic lesion.
